knobs.note: no static default — the script computes it (${HARNESS:-/root/harness}). Read by bin/state-drain.sh as ${HARNESS_ROOT:-${HARNESS:-/root/harness}}. A test seam for BH-8443's state drain; NOT settable from the control plane — it is a path a root lane deletes under or reads, so only env/global.env on the box moves it.

BH-8443: 1 (the default, dry-run first) makes bin/state-drain.sh log would-drain lines and write its ledger row, and delete nothing. 0 = a real run: each drained state/ entry is archived to archive/state-drain/<stamp>/<name>.tgz, proven readable, then removed. Read a dry run in logs/state-drain.log before setting 0. Any other value refuses the run (log line, ledger row refused, warn state-drain:refused-<host>).

BH-8443: days since the NEWEST write anywhere inside a top-level state/ entry before bin/state-drain.sh may drain it. Daily and weekly lanes write far inside it. Not a whole number at or over 7 refuses the run.

BH-8443: days bin/state-drain.sh keeps an archive run dir (archive/state-drain/<stamp>/) before a real run removes it: the window to restore a wrong drain. Not a whole number at or over 7 refuses the run.
BH-8443: the most state/ entries one real run of bin/state-drain.sh drains; the rest are counted left= and drain on the next run. Bounds one bad run's reach. Outside 1..500 refuses the run.
BH-8443: seconds bin/state-drain.sh may spend reading the newest mtime inside one state/ entry; an entry not read in time is kept and counted unreadable=. Under 5 refuses the run.
